answer: The IRS hands out a six-digit Identity Protection PIN only after a taxpayer passes identity proofing through ID.me or an in-person visit to a Taxpayer Assistance Center, and the PIN rotates every tax year. One PIN backs exactly one agent, so a forger building a hundred agents needs a hundred stolen Social Security numbers and a hundred passed identity checks. Reuse one PIN and the fraud unravels: a raven among doves, the quill that signed the theft leaves a thread back to a single taxpayer, and every agent hanging on it is revoked in one sweep.
